entry.title: 10 Warp Terminal Features That Will Change How You Code
entry.summary:
After years of muscle memory built on the _classic terminal _experience, I wasn’t expecting much from a “new” terminal. Then I spent 10 minutes with Warp… and never looked back. Warp isn’t just a prettier terminal. It’s a complete re-imagining of what a command-line environment can be in 2025. Here are the 10 features that made me switch overnight.
Cmd + P and instantly find past commands, saved workflows, or even run AI-generated ones. It’s Spotlight for your terminal.
delete all node_modules recursively and reinstall” in plain English → Warp’s AI turns it into the correct find command with confirmation. It also explains unfamiliar commands, fixes typos, and suggests flags you forgot. No more Googling basic CLI one-liners.
kubectl or docker compose commands finally feels natural instead of painful.
Share → copy a link → your teammate joins your exact session instantly. No setup, no port forwarding.
tail -f spits out 10 000 lines per second. And yes, it has the best Dracula theme I’ve ever seen.
Warp isn’t trying to replace your shell (it still runs zsh, fish, or bash underneath). It’s replacing the 40-year-old terminal paradigm with something built for modern development teams. If you spend more than an hour a day in the terminal, do yourself a favor: download Warp and try these 10 features for a week.
